changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-visible-predicates-5594.md`

- names `renderers/form/form.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#2212 recorded this exact symptom and PR #2214 fixed it — in a **different chain**: `ModalForm` → `resolveFormViewLayout` → `@object-ui/plugin-form` `sectionFields.ts` → `@object-ui/components` `renderers/form/form.tsx`. `FormPage.tsx` is on that chain at no point, and #2212's regression pin lives with the chain it fixed, so nothing in the suite could see this copy. One contract, two implementations, each only ever checked against itself.

### `.changeset/plugin-form-readme-classname-quantifier-5131.md`

- names `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `README.md`'s "Not a `FormField` key" table said a field-level `className` is "read on exactly one pseudo-field, `type: 'section-divider'`". That quantifier holds only for the renderer's *explicit* read — `className={fp.className}` on the `section-divider` branch of `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`. The same renderer forwards every key it did not destructure, and `className` is not among the names taken off the field config, not among the ones `stripRendererOnlyProps` removes, and so rides `{...fieldProps}` into `renderFieldComponent`, whose built-in `input` branch spreads it onto `ANGLE-BRACKETS(Input)`. A field-level `className` therefore lands visibly on ordinary built-in controls, and a reader taking "exactly one" literally concludes the opposite of what the code does (objectui#5131).

### `.changeset/text-input-description-aria-describedby-5735.md`

- names `renderers/form/form.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Before this the paragraph and the input were siblings with no programmatic relationship: a screen reader moving to the field announced the label and the value and never the helper text. The `label` half of the same block was already wired (`htmlFor` against the input's `id`), which is what made the gap specific to `description` rather than a general absence of a11y wiring — and the identical key authored on a field INSIDE `renderers/form/form.tsx` has been announced all along, so one authoring key behaved two ways depending on which container the author reached for. It no longer does.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `9fd6c2c6f` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1765 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2371 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36623051288)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f9a8e349c3ff6ecac92c8582247a1193e7c949c2`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11116 (body + 3 comments: triage `5893751796`, claim `5895889022`, os-dev-report `5897690904`), PR #11139 (body, 4 files, net diff against `main`), the 42 check-runs on the head (`filter=latest`), and head-ref reads of `form.tsx`, `packages/fields/src/field-type-alias.ts`, `field-type-alias.multiple.test.ts`, `widgets/MultiSelectField.tsx`, `widgets/SelectField.tsx`, `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, `packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts`, `packages/types/src/form.ts`, `fields-select/multi-select.json` and the three package manifests.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Route site — right.** `applyDeclaredArity` wraps the field row's `resolvedType` (`form.tsx:2837`, `applyDeclaredArity(widget || fieldProps.field?.widget || type, fieldProps.multiple)`). Every reader of that binding sees the routed id: `isOptionField` (`:2855`), `resolveFieldLabelling` (`:2923`), `resolvesToRegisteredFieldWidget` (`:2964`), `rendersBuiltinSelectEmptyState` (`:3008`), the `renderFieldComponent` call (`:3088`) and the default-placeholder read (`:3107`). `multiple` survives the field-row destructure (`:2597-2614` takes off `name`/`label`/`type`/`widget`/... and leaves the rest on `fieldProps`), so the key is read from the same object the file/image widgets read it from.
2. **Mirrors — right.** With `field:multiselect` as the resolved id: `resolveFieldLabelling` skips the `BUILTIN_FIELD_TYPES` short-circuit and reads `getMeta('multiselect','field').labelling`, which the fields index declares `'group'` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:4223`), so the label goes IDREF; `resolvesToRegisteredFieldWidget` takes the colon branch (`startsWith('field:') && !!ComponentRegistry.get(type)`); `rendersBuiltinSelectEmptyState` answers `false` (not builtin), so no `for` suppression competes with the group association. Routing inside `renderFieldComponent` alone would have left the label pointing a `for` at a chip row; the PR's components pin asserts exactly that mirror.
3. **Reached through `ComponentRegistry`, no new import — right.** The diff adds no import; `hasOwn` is the file's existing module-local helper (`:322`). `renderFieldComponent('field:multiselect', …)` resolves the widget at render time through the same `!BUILTIN_FIELD_TYPES.has(type) → ComponentRegistry.get(type)` path every `field:*` widget takes (`:3946-3954`). `packages/components/package.json` still has no `@object-ui/fields` dependency; `fields` depends on `components`, so the direction is preserved.
4. **`multiple` read truthy like `mapFieldTypeToFormType` — right.** `applyDeclaredArity` is `multiple && hasOwn(table, type) ? table[type] : type`; the fields side is `config?.multiple && MULTI_VALUE_FORM_TYPES[fieldType]`. Absent, `false`, `null` and `undefined` all leave the built-in select in place, pinned by the components `it.each` and the catalog without-`multiple` case. An object-bound field that already arrives as `field:multiselect` or `field:select` is not in the table and passes through unchanged, so the object-bound path is untouched (idempotent, like the fields pin `is idempotent for the type that is already inherently multi`).
5. **Cascade / option pre-filter — right, unchanged in kind.** `CASCADE_OPTION_WIDGET_TYPES` in core holds `select`, `multiselect`, `radio`, `checkboxes` (`optionRules.ts:292`), so `normalizeFieldType('field:multiselect')` keeps `isOptionField` true: the render-path `resolveCascadingOptions` narrowing, `emptyHint` and `dependentValues` forwarding (`:890`) all still apply to the routed field, the same as the object-bound path. The mount-time cascade-clear effect (`:1968`) still resolves the raw `select` and already handles array values (`isValueStillOffered(current, visible)`, then `Array.isArray(current) ? [] : null`), so an authored multi-select with `dependsOn`/`visibleWhen` is pruned per element by the widget and cleared as an array by the host, never coerced to a scalar.
6. **Submitted value is an array — right.** The value never passes through `BuiltinSelectControl`; `MultiSelectField` calls `onChange(string[])` and the catalog pin drives the real widget through the real `SchemaRenderer` to `onSubmit({ tags: ['frontend','devops'] })`. No second multi-select implementation exists inside `BuiltinSelectControl` (the diff touches neither it nor the `case 'select'` branch).
7. **Unregistered host (`@object-ui/components` without `@object-ui/fields`) — right, under the triage's one-path ruling.** `field:multiselect` resolves to nothing, so the routed field takes the `default` branch's `Input type="text"` (`:4310-4335`: `inputType || NATIVE_INPUT_FIELD_TYPES[declaredType] || 'text'`), and `resolveFieldLabelling` falls to `'control'` so the `for` lands on a labelable input. That is byte-for-byte what an authored `field:multiselect` (the object-bound spelling) renders in that host. The alternative, falling back to the built-in single-value select when the widget is absent, would reinstate the defect (a control that drops the declared arity) as a second answer on one path. The pin asserts parity with the authored spelling rather than a literal element, which is the right shape for a claim about the renderer's standing fallback. Noted, not a finding: for a components-only host a hand-authored `select` + `multiple` changes from a wrong-arity combobox to the renderer's generic text input; the changeset says so.
8. **The one-entry copy of `MULTI_VALUE_FORM_TYPES` — acceptable, not a finding.** Both tables hold exactly `select → field:multiselect` at the head. They are keyed in different spaces (the components table by `BUILTIN_FIELD_TYPES` members; the fields table by spec field types), and they coincide only because `select` is spelled the same in both, so a shared table hoisted to `@object-ui/core` (the objectui#4914 precedent for `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES`) would conflate two keyspaces, add a public export to a third package and a `minor` changeset, and leave this claim's file surface. The hand-authored path already resolves bare names without the fields `typeMap` at all (a hand-authored `tree` is not an object-bound `field:lookup`), so the pair's drift risk is a pre-existing property of the two paths, not one this diff creates. Drift on the one entry that matters is caught end to end by the catalog pin (real fields + real renderer). The table's docblock and the PR's Acceptance notes record the copy and say `keep them in step`. Escalated to the seat as a note only: if a second `MULTI_VALUE_FORM_TYPES` entry ever lands in `fields` for a `BUILTIN_FIELD_TYPES` member, the components table needs the same entry.
9. **Pins — match the triage.** `multi-select.json` renders multi-value markup (one `aria-pressed` toggle per option inside a `role=group` labelled by IDREF, no combobox) and submits an array; the same field without `multiple` is unchanged (combobox present, no toggles). The catalog example itself is untouched (`multiple` not deleted). The components pin covers routing, the label mirror, the submitted array, absent/`false`, and unregistered-host parity, with the precondition (`field:multiselect` unregistered) asserted rather than assumed.
10. **Public surface.** `BUILTIN_MULTI_VALUE_WIDGETS` and `applyDeclaredArity` are module-private (no `export`); no type, prop, schema or accepted key moves. `FormField` already carries `[key: string]: any` (`types/form.ts:1877`), so `fieldProps.multiple` type-checks with or without PR objectui#11115, which touches `packages/types` only (disjoint files, per the triage).

Gate verdicts on the head (`filter=latest`, read complete at 20:11Z): 43 runs, 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard)`, `dependabot` — none applies to a PR head), 0 failure, 0 in progress. All eight `Test (shard N/8)`, `Test`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Control Byte Scan` and the five changeset gates are `success`. The dev report's local readings (form dir 68 files / 465 passed, catalog 35 files / 2203 passed, ablation 6 red / 4 green on the predicted split) are consistent with them and were not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` — right. No accept-set, schema, prop or type moves; an already-declared key (`multiple`, on `FormField` via its index signature today and by name once objectui#11115 lands) takes effect on one more branch of the renderer, and the two module-level additions are not exported.

Changeset `.changeset/11116-builtin-select-multiple.md`: `'@object-ui/components': patch` — right. The diff publishes a behaviour fix in `@object-ui/components` only. `examples/schema-catalog` is `private: true` (`@object-ui/example-schema-catalog`), so its new test needs no entry; `packages/fields`, `packages/core` and `packages/types` are untouched. The paragraph names what changes (the routed widget, the group label association, the array, the unchanged no-`multiple` case, the unregistered-host fallback) without overclaiming. `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report` and `Changeset Claim Re-read` are all `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 — catalog type-check narrowed locally.** Answered by the head's `Type Check` run (`success`), which covers the full catalog test program; the local narrowing is disclosed in the PR body and the report and changes nothing about what CI measured.
- **Deviation 2 — the catalog pin is a new file.** `examples/schema-catalog/test/` is the catalog's existing render-test home (35 test files ran there at the head), and the claim's surface reads `plus a catalog render pin if the catalog has a render-test home`. In surface; accepted.
